walkthroughs.body_html:
The American Dream: Reality & Illusion 1945-1980 — a core area of A-Level History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The American Dream: Reality & Illusion 1945-1980 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The American Dream: Reality & Illusion 1945-1980.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Did the Wall Street Crash cause the Great Depression?
options: It triggered it but the underlying causes were over-production, agricultural slump, weak banking regulation, and uneven wealth — the Crash exposed structural problems.
Because Britain banned them from owning land west of the Atlantic.
The Wall Street Crash on its own caused the Great Depression.
The Wall Street Crash happened because the US joined WWII.
Ideological incompatibility plus mutual suspicion after WWII — disputes over Eastern Europe, the atomic bomb, and broken wartime agreements.
Because Britain banned them from owning land west of the Atlantic.
It began when the USSR shot down a US spy plane.
Stalin started it by invading Eastern Europe after the war.

mcqs.q: Why did the American colonies rebel against Britain?
options: Because Britain banned them from owning land west of the Atlantic.
The Wall Street Crash happened because the US joined WWII.
Disputes over taxation without representation after the Seven Years' War, growing colonial identity, and British attempts to tighten imperial control on previously autonomous colonies.
The colonists rebelled because they were heavily oppressed and impoverished.
